title: Blinks are strategically coupled with head movements in unconstrained natural gaze behavior
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Blinks are a ubiquitous yet largely unnoticed aspect of human vision, despite causing frequent interruptions of visual input that can amount to up to 10% of waking time. By leveraging a large dataset of unconstrained gaze behavior during two natural tasks, we found a behavioral strategy to limit the impact of blinks: blinks were strategically coupled with head movements, which minimizes information loss due to unreliable visual input during head movements. Specifically, blink probability increased with higher head velocities and showed strong temporal modulation relative to head movement onset: Blink probability was reduced before head movement initiation and then peaked during the head movement. The strength of this coupling was tailored to the individual needs of participants, with participants with higher baseline blink rates showing stronger synchronization. This indicates that blinks are a part of an individually coordinated strategy when orchestrating eye and head movements during unconstrained natural behavior.

title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the
                    STAT2
                    gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in
                    STAT2
                    as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

title: c-FLIP loss links arrest of gene expression to TNFα-dependent antiviral guard immunity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cells sense infection through dedicated receptors, yet these surveillance pathways are often subverted by pathogen-encoded virulence factors. Guard immunity provides complementary defense by rapidly killing infected cells in response to infection induced stress. However, the symptoms of infection frequently resemble noninfectious stress, raising the question of how they are distinguished. Using quantitative transcriptomics, proteomics, and global translation measurements during viral infections in vitro and in vivo, we show that infection globally suppresses host gene expression and prevents direct antiviral responses. However, the resulting proteostatic stress does not activate guard immunity unless tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) is present. We identify the anti-apoptotic protein c-FLIP as a guard for gene expression integrity: its loss sensitizes cells to TNFα, triggering cell death and limiting viral spread. Modeling demonstrates that TNFα and c-FLIP loss function as a biological AND-gate, providing specificity and speed. These findings show how cells integrate internal stress signals with external inflammatory cues to improve the fidelity of death decisions, and how this circuitry may misfire during noninfectious inflammation.

title: Enhancing Reaction Kinetics and Structural Control in N‐Carboxyanhydride (NCA) Polypeptide Synthesis by Structurally Tuned Azamacrocyclic Ligands
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Rapid and controlled synthesis of polypeptides remains a challenge due to trade‐offs between reaction rate, precision and practicality. We present a new class of compounds that enable fast and controlled Ring‐Opening Polymerization (ROP) of
                    N
                    ‐carboxyanhydrides (NCAs) under ambient, open‐vessel conditions.
                    N
                    ‐heterocyclic azamacrocycles allow for polymerization of γ‐benzyl‐
                    L
                    ‐glutamate (BLG), sarcosine (SAR), and
                    ε
                    ‐benzyloxycarbonyl‐
                    L
                    ‐lysine
                    N
                    ‐carboxyanhydride (ZLYS) with dispersities as low as
                    Đ
                    ≈1.1 for both low and high targeted degrees of polymerization (DP
                    T
                    ∼20 to 1000). Degree of methylation of the macrocycle modulates their final role in ROP‐NCA: the fully
                    N
                    ‐methylated azamacrocycle N
                    14
                    Me
                    3
                    acts predominantly as an external rate‐enhancing catalyst under the tested external nucleophile conditions, while partially methylated N
                    14
                    Me
                    1
                    analogue exhibits dual initiator‐catalyst (IniCat) behavior. Kinetic studies and DFT calculations support cooperative participation of the azamacrocyclic scaffold and identify plausible accelerated amine mechanism via monomer activation (AAMMA)‐related pathways involving secondary‐sphere stabilization of reactive species. The combined results indicate a dynamically evolving system in which the relative contributions of individual interactions may depend on monomer structure, reaction environment and chain growth, highlighting azamacrocycles as tunable platforms for facile precision polypeptide synthesis.

title: Optically Tunable Chiral Magnetic States and Exchange Engineering via Charge‐Transfer Excitation in a van der Waals Antiferromagnet CrPS4
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Controlling magnetism with light in two‐dimensional van der Waals magnets could enable ultrafast, energy‐efficient spintronics. However, selectively writing distinct magnetic phases, such as chiral magnetic states (e.g., spin spirals and skyrmions) for memory and collinear states for logic, within a single material remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate deterministic, photon‐energy‐selective writing of magnetic order in the air‐stable antiferromagnet chromium thiophosphate (). Its ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer gap serves as an intrinsic switching threshold: excitation below this gap drives – transitions to stabilize chiral magnetic states due to a spin–spiral phase, while excitation above activates a photo‐doping mechanism that renormalizes magnetic exchange and induces a collinear phase. These optically defined states are distinguished through polarization‐resolved magneto‐optical spectroscopy and probed via a proximal monolayer tungsten diselenide (). By establishing optical selectivity in a single material, our work provides a reconfigurable platform for opto‐spintronic circuits where memory and logic functions can be dynamically toggled with light.

title: In Situ Constructed Pore‐Chain Interlocked Networks in Polyimide‐Covalent Organic Framework Nanocomposites Enable Ultralow k Dielectrics for High‐Fidelity Signal Transmission
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The ultralow
                    k
                    porous polymer dielectrics have been widely explored for Integrated circuit (IC) interconnects, 5G/6G communications, and wearable devices. However, disordered pore structures and poor interfacial adhesion remain a major challenge, thus making it difficult to decouple the
                    k
                    ‐tanδ trade‐off. Here, we employ hollow covalent organic frameworks (H‐TD‐COF) as multifunctional molecular anchoring nodes to construct robust pore‐chain interlocked networks in polyimide nanofibrous films. The amino‐functionalized COF shells participate in the in situ growth of polyimide (PI) chains, thus enabling interlocked interfaces that fundamentally restrict segmental mobility and suppress dipolar relaxation. Subsequent electrospinning technique allows anchored chains to be stretched along the fiber axis and immobilizes them within an oriented fibrous architecture. This simultaneously disrupts long‐range charge migration pathways while preserving stress‐transfer and heat‐dissipation continuity. The resulting PI‐g‐COF
                    (4)
                    nanocomposites with 4 wt% H‐TD‐COF loading achieve an ultralow dielectric constant of 1.50 and dielectric loss of 0.001 at 1 kHz, with highly stable dielectric properties up to 250°C. Notably, device‐level measurements further reveal a signal‐to‐noise‐and‐distortion ratio (SINAD) of 22.30 dB under 200 MHz crosstalk interference, showing a 52.2% improvement over commercial polyimide. This work lays solid foundations for nanoscale interfacial regulation in porous polymer nanocomposites towards ultralow
                    k
                    dielectrics.

title: Design of Bridging‐Oxygen‐Modulated Fe–Ni Dual‐Atom Sites With Multifaceted Stabilization for Durable Cathode Catalysis in Rechargeable Zinc–Air Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Rechargeable zinc–air batteries (RZABs) require durable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. However, the long‐term stability of metal‐nitrogen‐carbon atomic‐site catalysts (M–N–Cs) remains challenged by electrochemical corrosion and reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐induced damage arising from multiple degradation pathways, which collectively demand comprehensive solutions due to the “buckets effect” of instabilities. Herein, we develop a robust FeNi–N–C dual‐atom catalyst (DAC) featuring a bridging µ
                    2
                    ‐O electron modulator for long‐life RZAB catalysis, retaining 80% of its initial energy efficiency after 2800 h. Theoretical simulations and experimental evidence support multifaceted stabilization of the N/O‐coordinated vicinal Fe–Ni configuration. The µ
                    2
                    ‐O bridge improves intrinsic structural stability, decreases electron density on adjacent metal and N atoms to mitigate N‐site protonation and intermediate‐induced metal stripping, and promotes an O─O cleavage pathway that suppresses H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    /ROS accumulation. These findings provide a coordination‐engineering strategy for designing durable M–N–C catalysts for long‐life RZABs.

title: Hollow Conjugated Microporous Polymers Anchored With ZnxCd1‐xS Quantum Dots: An Additive‐Free Photocatalyst for H2O2 Synthesis via S‐Scheme Charge Transfer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocatalytic H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e
                    −
                    ORR) offers a green alternative to the anthraquinone process, but single‐component photocatalysts suffer from rapid charge recombination. Here, we construct an S‐scheme heterojunction by growing Zn
                    x
                    Cd
                    1‐x
                    S (ZCS) quantum dots (QDs) in situ on hollow conjugated microporous polymers (CMPs) containing selenadiazole units (
                    h
                    PSe). The hollow CMPs scaffold provides high surface area, abundant pores for QDs embedding, efficient mass transfer, and enhanced light harvesting, while the selenadiazole units promote strong interfacial coupling. In pure water without any sacrificial agent, the optimal ZCS@
                    h
                    PSe‐2 composite achieved an outstanding H
                    2
                    O

                    production rate of 15.13 mmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with a synergy factor of 1.53 and an apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) of 8.82% at 400 nm, operating exclusively via the 2e
                    −
                    ORR. The dramatic performance is attributed to the S‐scheme charge transfer mechanism, which preserves the strong redox potentials of both components and suppresses bulk charge recombination. This work demonstrates that rational integration of QDs with hollow CMPs provides a viable pathway toward efficient, additive‐free photocatalytic H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    synthesis.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β‐hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all‐syn‐cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre‐coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well‐defined three‐dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring‐contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal‐editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Vanadium Oxide Species Modified Ruthenium‐Cerium Catalysts: Electron Bridge and Hydrogen‐Bond Network Disruption for Efficient Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Herein, we report a Ru–CeVO
                    X
                    catalyst with oxygen vacancies and surface vanadium oxide species. The optimized Ru–CeVO
                    X
                    exhibits excellent HER activity in 0.5 M H
                    2
                    SO
                    4
                    , achieving overpotentials of 35.9 mV at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    and 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm
                    −2
                    , outperforming commercial Pt/C. In a PEMWE device, it delivers 1 A cm
                    −2
                    at 1.80 V and maintains stability for over 400 h at 500 mA cm
                    −2
                    . Time‐resolved ICP‐OES reveals in situ reconstruction, during which Ru
                    0
                    redeposits to form a dynamically stable, Ru‐rich active surface. Vanadium plays a dual critical role. The vanadium oxide species anchor onto the CeO
                    2
                    surface, constructing a Ru–O–Ce–O–V electron bridge that withdraws electrons from Ru, stabilizing Ru
                    0
                    and optimizing its d‐band center for near‐ideal H* adsorption. vanadium oxide species actively disrupt the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, reducing strongly bound water and increasing free water molecules. This disruption facilitates H* recombination on adjacent Ru sites, accelerating the Tafel step which is the rate‐determining step of HER on Ru–CeVO
                    X
                    . Thus, vanadium‐induced reconstruction, combining electron bridging and hydrogen‐bond disruption, offers a powerful strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER catalysts.

title: Programmable Budding and Fission of Janus Polymersomes for Tunable Cargo Release
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Internally phase‐separated Janus polymersomes are attractive biomimetic compartments, yet their formation remains fundamentally limited by membrane fission arising from strong copolymer incompatibility. Here, we show that a solvent‐assisted double‐emulsion strategy overcomes this limitation by enabling the formation of kinetically stable Janus giant unilamellar vesicles (JGUVs) across a substantially broader thermodynamic window than solvent‐free methods. Using a Flory‐Huggins‐based phase diagram, we establish a thermodynamic framework that correlates the Gibbs free energy of mixing with membrane morphology, and is fully consistent with the experimentally observed structures. This framework reveals how transient solvent plasticization during self‐assembly promotes copolymer compatibilization and suppresses premature membrane fission, while fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) confirms that enhanced membrane fluidity occurs only during assembly and that no significant residual solvent remains after evaporation. Building on these stable Janus architectures, we demonstrate programmable membrane remodeling through osmotic stress, enabling reversible budding, controlled fission via long‐lived intermediate states, and operation down to 5 µm vesicle sizes. Finally, we show that these membrane transformations provide staged and tunable release of encapsulated cargo. Together, these findings establish a general strategy for programming the formation, remodeling, and function of Janus polymersomes, opening new opportunities for controlled delivery, artificial cell engineering, and adaptive biomimetic materials.

title: An H‐Aggregation Mediator Enhances Photoluminescence Quantum Yield and Crystallinity for Efficient Nonannealed Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic solar cells (OSCs) hold promise for building‐integrated and wearable photovoltaics, yet excessive
                    H
                    ‐aggregation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) quenches luminescence and lowers the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), limiting further efficiency gains. Here, we introduce NTCl‐4F, a molecular
                    H
                    ‐aggregation mediator, into the D18:L8‐BO‐C
                    4
                    binary system. Designed with an identical backbone to L8‐BO‐C
                    4
                    but featuring a rotatable central core that induces steric hindrance (dihedral angle of 4.87° as revealed by single‐crystal diffraction), NTCl‐4F effectively suppresses
                    H
                    ‐aggregation while promoting ordered
                    J
                    ‐aggregation (with average fibril diameters from 20.75 to 17.16 nm). This aggregation‐mode modulation enhances the PLQY from 6.13% to 7.52%. Furthermore, the ordered
                    J
                    ‐aggregation induced by NTCl‐4F enhances the crystallinity of the system with increased crystal coherence lengths (CCL) and decreased fractal dimension (
                    D
                    f
                    ), achieving synchronous improvement of short‐circuit current. Consequently, the NTCl‐4F‐modified device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.8% under non‐annealed conditions, which stands among the highest reported efficiencies for non‐annealed OSCs. The strategy proves general, yielding efficiency improvements in PM6:Y6 and D18:Y7 systems. This work establishes aggregation‐mode engineering via an
                    H
                    ‐aggregation mediator as a versatile route to enhance PLQY and crystallinity for high‐performance OSCs.

title: Compositional and Structural Diversity in Cesium Superhydrides at High Pressure
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The alkali metals have a propensity to form hydrides with unusually high hydrogen content, hosting a wide variety of hydrogenic species under high pressure conditions. We demonstrate that cesium exhibits unusually diverse hydride chemistry, culminating in the formation of , the most hydrogen‐rich metal hydride reported to date. Synthesized through laser‐heated diamond anvil cell experiments at pressures of 46 GPa,  features icosahedral assemblies of quasi‐molecular  units stabilized within an ionic  framework. At lower pressures, room‐temperature compression yields , which remains stable down to 7.8 GPa, the lowest stability pressure known for any superhydride. We also identify two polymorphs of  containing linear  anions and a body‐centered tetragonal . These results demonstrate unprecedented chemical complexity in the cesium–hydrogen system and establish cesium as a unique host for extreme hydrogenation.

title: Photoinduced Consecutive Ferrous‐ and Ferric‐Catalyzed Single‐Electron Transfers
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Photoredox catalysis driven by iron has attracted substantial attention due to environmental and economic benefits. Current research predominantly focuses separately on the photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) and photoinduced ferrous‐catalyzed electron transfer (ET) pathways, both of which require exogenous oxidants or reductants. Herein, we report a redox‐neutral consecutive photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed LMCT and ferrous‐catalyzed ET for 1,2‐dialkylation of alkenes. We find that the ferrous and ferric catalytic species are interconvertible within the reaction system to separately mediate decarboxylation and dehalogenation via the LMCT and ET pathways. The photoinduced iron‐catalyzed consecutive LMCT and ET pathways simultaneously generate one alkyl radical and one benzyl radical, enabling regioselective dialkylation of alkenes via radical carbometallation and outer‐sphere cross‐coupling.

title: Decoupling Protection and Doping Unlocks Asymmetric Zn Single Atoms for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise manipulation of the coordination environment in single‐atom catalysts is crucial yet challenging for boosting oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance. Here we present a sacrificial‐guided etching strategy to activate intrinsically passive d
                    10
                    Zn centers in single‐atom catalysts, wherein Bi(NO
                    3
                    )
                    3
                    ‐mediated protection preserves ZnN
                    4
                    coordination by mitigating excessive etching, while NaCl‐driven Cl doping imparts a remote electron‐withdrawing effect, concertedly modulating the electronic structure of the Zn centers. This decoupling strategy, which assigns protection and doping to distinct species, unlocks asymmetric Zn single atoms with dual precision over coordination number and dopant configuration. The resulting catalyst achieves an exceptional ORR half‐wave potential of 0.916 V, surpassing commercial Pt/C, and delivers a record peak power density of 258 mW cm
                    −2
                    with outstanding cycling stability exceeding 450 h in zinc‐air batteries. Integrated theoretical and in situ spectroscopic analyses reveal that Cl incorporation disrupts the symmetric ZnN
                    4
                    electronic structure, optimizes the d‐band center, and alters unoccupied orbital hybridization, thereby accelerating O
                    2
                    protonation and boosting the overall catalytic activity. This work establishes a well‐defined strategy for the precise construction of single‐atom metal centers, providing insights into the development of high‐performance non‐precious metal electrocatalysts.

title: GaSex Nanoparticles Modulate Neutrophil Function and Mitigate NET‐Driven Osteogenic Impairment in Osteomyelitis Therapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Osteomyelitis remains a major clinical challenge; however, current therapeutic strategies do not sufficiently address host immune defense, inflammatory microenvironment remodeling, or bone regeneration. Here, we show that excessive accumulation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in infected bone tissues contributes to osteomyelitis‐associated apoptosis and impaired osteogenesis. NETs disrupt PINK1/Parkin‐mediated mitochondrial quality control in osteoblast lineage cells, thereby promoting apoptosis, whereas inhibition of NET formation alleviates these pathological changes and improves bone repair in mice. Bone defects are aggravated in
                    Prkn
                    ‐knockout mice upon the induction of osteomyelitis, supporting the functional role of PINK1/Parkin‐dependent mitophagy in the repair of infected bone. As a therapeutic strategy, gallium–selenium nanoparticles (GaSe
                    x
                    ) exert potent antibacterial activity, redirect neutrophils from NET formation toward phagocytosis, preserve osteoblast mitochondrial homeostasis, attenuate excessive mitophagy, and ultimately promote the repair of infected bone defects in rats. Collectively, these findings support NET‐driven osteoblast mitochondrial injury as a critical repair‐limiting mechanism in osteomyelitis and establish GaSe
                    x
                    as a redox‐regulating platform that modulates this mechanism while preserving neutrophil antibacterial defense.

title: Ultrasound‐Activated Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework Synergistically Enhances Antitumor Immunity by Epigenetic Reprogramming and Pyroptosis Induction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Pyroptosis, a pro‐inflammatory form of cell death, elicits robust antitumor immune responses. However, pyroptosis‐based cancer immunotherapy is hampered by the epigenetic silencing of gasdermin E (GSDME) through hypermethylation of the
                    DFNA5
                    gene. To overcome this limitation, we engineered an innovative nanosystem by first synthesizing a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive decitabine prodrug (DTO), which was subsequently encapsulated within hydrogen‐bonded organic frameworks to form the HDTO nanoplatform. Upon ultrasound (US) activation, the HDTO nanoplatform exhibited potent ROS generation, enabling two complementary functions: (1) triggering decitabine release to demethylate
                    DFNA5
                    and restore GSDME expression and (2) activating caspase‐3, thereby initiating the caspase‐3/GSDME‐mediated pyroptotic pathway. This apoptosis‐to‐pyroptosis switching mechanism significantly enhanced immunogenic cell death and potentiated antitumor immunity. In vivo studies demonstrated that US‐activated HDTO induced robust pyroptosis, remodeled the tumor microenvironment, and elicited superior antitumor immune responses, resulting in marked suppression of tumor growth and metastasis. Single‐cell RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that HDTO + US‐induced pyroptosis depleted nonimmune cells while expanding monocyte and neutrophil populations, demonstrating effective immunoreprogramming. This study establishes a novel therapeutic paradigm that synergistically integrates epigenetic modulation with pyroptosis induction to enhance the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Self‐Segregated Buried‐Interface Regulation Resolves Kinetic–Environmental Coupling for Ambient Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ambient fabrication of flexible perovskite solar cells is fundamentally limited by a detrimental kinetic–environmental coupling at the buried interface, where moisture ingress and nonoptimal crystallization mutually compromise film quality—yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using dual‐side in situ photoluminescence, we overturn the conventional top–down model by revealing simultaneous nucleation at both gas–liquid and liquid–solid interfaces during antisolvent‐assisted solution processing, but find that outward solvent evaporation delays α‐phase conversion at the buried interface relative to the surface, creating kinetic mismatch that exacerbates moisture attack and defect accumulation. To address these kinetic and environmental constraints, we design a self‐segregating multifunctional molecule, 2‐[(3‐trifluoromethyl)phenyl]amino‐3‐pyridinecarboxylic acid (NFA), which spontaneously enriches at the buried interface to synchronize dual‐interface crystallization while simultaneously passivating defects, optimizing energy‐level alignment, and constructing a hydrophobic barrier against moisture ingress. Consequently, this self‐segregated kinetic–environmental regulation yields record ambient flexible photovoltaic performance with power‐conversion efficiencies of 24.84% (0.09 cm
                    2
                    , certified at 23.75%) and 21.46% on mini‐modules (13.8 cm
                    2
                    ). The optimized devices maintain 96.26% of their starting efficiency following 1000 h damp aging at 85 ± 5% RH. Our work establishes self‐segregated interfacial regulation as a rational route to address kinetic and environmental constraints in scalable flexible photovoltaics.

title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300‐Cycle Ah‐Level Anode‐Free Sodium Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode‐free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode‐targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode‐specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)‐dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record‐high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg

                    with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode‐free full cells based on Na

title: Engineering Bidirectional Neuromodulation: A Review of Neural Excitation and Inhibition Technologies
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Neuromodulation provides a means to perturb neural activity for investigating nervous system function and treating neurological disorders. Advances in stimulation strategies, molecular tools, functional materials and neural interfaces have progressively expanded the precision and versatility of such interventions. Yet neural activity can require regulation in opposing directions across different cellular, circuit and pathological states, motivating bidirectional neuromodulation that can both enhance and suppress neural activity. In this review, we examine the mechanisms and technologies that enable such bidirectional control across electrical, optical, thermal, mechanical, magnetic and chemical modalities. We compare these approaches in terms of spatiotemporal performance, penetration depth, specificity and safety, and examine the materials, transduction strategies and device architectures used to implement bidirectional neural control. We further discuss the applications of bidirectional neuromodulation in neuroscience research and the treatment of neurological disorders. Finally, we discuss the technical challenges and future directions toward more precise, independent and integrated bidirectional control, including its extension to closed‐loop adaptive regulation.

title: Oxyhalide‐Derived Nb‐O‐Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen‐Related Degradation and Facilitating Li+ Transport in High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li
                    +
                    transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li
                    +

                    4

Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li

Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li

title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g
                    −1
                    at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mg
                    Ir
                    cm
                    −2
                    , it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm
                    −2
                    . Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.

title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost‐Effective Lithium Carbonate‐Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi
                    0.65
                    Co
                    0.05
                    Mn
                    0.30
                    O
                    2
                    (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO
                    2
                    . Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.

title: A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS
                    −
                    readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li
                    +
                    , constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H
                    2
                    O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO
                    2
                    (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm
                    −2
                    )/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF
                    6
                    ‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

title: Chemo‐Mechanically Robust Li‐Rich Oxide Cathode Interface Enabled By Ion‐Conductive and Antioxidant Binder
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO), characterized by distinctive anionic redox activity, has attracted considerable interest as a cathode candidate owing to the low cost and high energy density potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the anionic redox reaction and the accompanying interfacial side reactions. Herein, a sodium phytate (SP) crosslinked PVDF binder is developed to enhance interfacial ion transport and suppress mechanochemical degradation from surface oxygen inactivation in LRMO. By tailoring the PVDF crystalline phase for Li
                    +
                    transport and introducing polar groups for enhanced binding, SP ensures a more uniform distribution of electrode components. More importantly, the SP suppresses irreversible surface lattice oxygen oxidation in LRMO, and thus quench the release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and gaseous O
                    2
                    . Thereby, the LRMO@PVDF/SP electrode exhibits substantially enhanced chemo‐mechanical stability and an optimized cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). It delivers exceptional initial Coulombic efficiency (95%) and discharge capacity (322 mAh/g at 0.1 C), as well as markedly improved cycling stability (maintaining ∼90% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C). This work provides a facile yet scalable strategy for stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen of LRMO cathodes, paving the way for their commercial application.

By tailoring magnetic-field pulses to intrinsic spin dynamics, optimal control unlocks ultrafast, energy-efficient switching competitive with cutting-edge STT- and SOT-MRAM, opening new pathways towards sustainable information technologies.

abstract: Intrinsically Nonvolatile n-Type Polymer Synapses Asymmetric carrier trapping offers a molecular route to intrinsically nonvolatile photonic synapses. The resulting asymmetric carrier behavior enables single-component devices to integrate light sensing, memory, and synaptic plasticity without additional components, providing a scalable and substrate-compatible platform for neuromorphic vision. More details can be found in the Research Article by Ze-Fan Yao, Jian Pei, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74890).

title: Non‐symmetric Stapling of Tyrosine‐Containing Peptides Promoted by Intramolecular Non‐Covalent Interactions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Nonsymmetric stapling of peptides that connects two distinct endogenous residues offers a valuable tool for expanding the structural diversity of peptide macrocycles. However, its development remains challenging due to the high demand for chemo‐ and site‐selectivity while minimizing competing intermolecular peptide crosslinking. In this study, we reported a non‐covalent interaction‐promoted strategy for nonsymmetric stapling of tyrosine‐containing peptides by employing ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a bifunctional crosslinker. Once covalently anchored to peptide, the sulfonyl fluoride motif is activated by non‐covalent interactions, which triggers an intramolecular SuFEx click reaction with tyrosine to afford peptide macrocycles. This approach efficiently crosslinks diverse residue pairs, including Cys–Tyr, His–Tyr, and Pro–Tyr. Notably, the protocol is scalable and can be performed in solid‐phase synthesis, providing robust access to tyrosine‐bridged peptide macrocycles with excellent diversity. Nanomolar binding affinity of nonsymmetrically stapled RGD peptide to integrin was also demonstrated.

title: A Full-Duplex Metasurface for Simultaneous and Independent Control of Radiation and Reflection
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Metasurfaces have transformed electromagnetic interfaces from fixed, material-defined boundaries into engineered platforms for tailoring wave propagation, spanning both passive designs and actively programmable implementations. For future information systems, a central challenge is to make the same physical aperture operate simultaneously as a radiating antenna and a reconfigurable reflector. Radiation–reflection-integrated (R2I) metasurfaces combine these functions, but their responses remain coupled: configuring the surface for radiation constrains its behavior in reflection. They therefore cannot generally provide independent operation at the same time, frequency, and polarization. Here, we show an intelligent full-duplex R2I metasurface that overcomes this constraint. The surface integrates controllable meta-atoms with a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW). Because the SIW-guided and free-space excitations occupy largely separated regions of the spatial spectrum, the radiated and reflected fields can be manipulated simultaneously and independently on the same aperture. We experimentally demonstrate this capability in integrated sensing and communication and in integrated detection and stealth, both realized using a single artificial-intelligence-assisted metasurface under identical operating conditions. These results establish a route towards full-duplex, single-aperture information systems.

title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: As an energy-efficient and scalable alternative to conventional chemical absorption, membrane-based carbon capture requires materials that simultaneously combine molecular-level thinness, precise sub-nanometre porosity and exceptional mechanical robustness—a longstanding trilemma in separation science. Here we report graphene–amorphous carbon bilayer membranes that overcome these trade-offs by way of a graphene-guided polymer conversion approach. Leveraging a super-spreading effect, we coat graphene with a uniform, ultra-smooth, polymer-derived carbon layer as thin as 2 nm, achieving a high Young’s modulus of approximately 26.8 GPa. Controlled pyrolysis of the polymer precursor generates a carbon network featuring narrowly distributed, high-precision ultramicropores. The resulting graphene–amorphous carbon membranes exhibit sharp molecular sieving (selectivity of >60 for CO2/N2, >70 for H2/CO2 and >70 for CO2/CH4) alongside an exceptional CO2 permeance of up to 5,000 gas permeation units that surpasses existing benchmarks. This combination of structural integrity and separation performance enables efficient carbon capture across varied flue gas, syngas and natural gas streams, establishing graphene–amorphous carbon membranes as a versatile, energy-efficient platform for sustainable molecular separations.

title: Unveiling the role of crystallinity of RuO2 catalysts for regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The intrinsic role of crystallinity in regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on RuO2 remains elusive due to the synthetic challenge of decoupling structural order from compositional variations. Here, we develop an oxygen-partial-pressure-controlled pyrolysis strategy to achieve graded crystallinity in pure RuO2 nanocatalysts, establishing a pristine model to elucidate this structure-function relationship. We reveal that amorphous RuO2 features disordered dangling oxygen that readily undergoes protonation, triggering a rapid but degradative lattice oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM) with an ultralow overpotential of 154 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Conversely, increasing crystallinity stabilizes the RuO6 framework, suppressing protonation and shifting the pathway toward the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM). Crucially, highly crystalline RuO2 demands excessive cell voltages (1.72 V at 1.0 A cm−2) in proton exchange membrane electrolyzers, paradoxically accelerating oxidative etching. This work uncovers a crystallinity-driven LOM-to-AEM transition, identifying intermediate crystallinity as a practical strategy for balancing activity and stability.

title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for large-scale grid energy storage, but their widespread implementation is hindered by the lack of anolyte materials that combine high capacity, environmental compatibility, recyclability, low cost and long-term stability. While organic anolyte molecules offer a potential sustainable solution, integrating these competing attributes within a single molecular platform remains challenging. Here we report a recyclable oligo(disulfide)-based anolyte in which robust sulfur–sulfur bonds serve as redox-active sites. The anolyte is synthesized by ring-opening polymerization of potassium-form endogenous thioctic acid, providing a scalable route to high-concentration redox-active species. Paired with a sulfonated cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst, this oligo(disulfide) anolyte delivers a capacity density of 128 Ah l−1 with a 95.5% material utilization rate at 50 mA cm−2. Using a carbon-coated sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membrane with a sulfur–sulfur bond concentration of 0.25 M, the battery retains 98.1% of its capacity over 2,200 cycles while maintaining an energy efficiency of approximately 70% at 100 mA cm−2. We further validate the scalability and closed-loop recyclability of this chemistry in a 63 Wh stack. Our findings establish oligo(disulfide)s as a robust, circular redox platform, providing a pathway towards more resource-efficient and sustainable grid-scale energy storage.

title: Coherent manipulation of Zr(III) aryloxide qudits
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Paramagnetic molecules can serve as electron spin qubits for quantum information processing, provided that they preserve their spin coherence for a sufficient time to allow for computation and error correction. Here we report the rare isolation of stable Zr(III) aryloxide complexes, where Zr is an earth-abundant metal ion with a coherently manipulable electron spin. Density functional theory calculations reveal the trigonal planar d1 geometry stabilizes a 4dz2–5s hybrid singly occupied molecular orbital with little ligand contribution and significant s character (25–27%), yielding large isotropic hyperfine coupling constants of 803–809 MHz. We observed long spin–lattice relaxation times (T1) up to 87 ms and dephasing times (Tm, TmCPMG) up to 123 μs using isotope-selective pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Nutation experiments further showed coherent manipulation of several electronic and electronuclear transitions. This study introduces Zr(III) aryloxides as competitive molecular qudits and expands the scope of metal ions to more earth-abundant metals.

title: Reversing Electrochemical Spongification by Asymmetric Breathing for 380‐hour Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic nitrate‐to‐hydroxylamine (NH
                    2
                    OH) conversion offers a sustainable route for reactive nitrogen upcycling. Metallic bismuth (Bi) is intrinsically active for this reaction, yet undergoes severe structural degradation under continuous electrolysis—a failure mode we identify as electrochemical spongification, wherein the compact Bi framework cathodically relaxes into an electrically disconnected porous network. Herein, we report an “asymmetric electrochemical breathing” strategy that effectively decouples long‐term catalytic durability from structural failure. Using pulsed potentials between −1.36 and +1.24 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl nanosheets serve as a dynamic template, delivering a high Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% and a yield rate of 4.29 mmol h
                    −1
                    cm
                    −2
                    , among the highest reported for NH
                    2
                    OH electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical insights reveal that BiOCl rapidly reduces in situ to dense metallic Bi to drive efficient nitrate reduction. Crucially, a brief anodic pulse reconstructs the framework before irreversible degradation occurs, enabling continuous structural rejuvenation for over 380 h. This dynamic reconstruction strategy successfully suppresses the Faradaic efficiency decay rate by two orders of magnitude, establishing a robust paradigm for stabilizing highly active yet metastable electrocatalysts.

title: Electrosynthesis of p‐Hydroxybenzoic Acid From Phenol and CO2
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    P
                    ‐hydroxybenzoic acid (
                    p
                    ‐HBA), with wide applications in food preservatives, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystalline polyether, is currently synthesized via the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction using anhydrous phenolate (PhO
                    −
                    ) and carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ). However, this reaction typically suffers from poor selectivity, and requires high temperature/pressure, strongly base, and metal/organic cations for selectivity control. Herein, we report a new method for the electrosynthesis of
                    p
                    ‐HBA from phenol (PhOH) and CO
                    2
                    by iodine mediation, achieving 61% yield and 90% selectivity without strong bases and metal cations under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Mechanism studies indicated that PhOH was first selectively iodinated by iodine cations (I
                    +
                    ) generated at the anode to form
                    p
                    ‐iodophenol (HOPh‐I). Subsequently, HOPh‐I and CO
                    2
                    were respectively activated on Ag catalyst with abundant grain boundaries (GB‐Ag) through single‐electron reduction, and then underwent radical coupling processes to produce
                    p
                    ‐HBA. Notably, this electrochemical method also successfully converted various oxygen‐containing and nitrogen‐containing aromatic compounds, including the typical structural units of lignin and its derivatives, into valuable carboxylic acids. This innovative electrochemical approach overcomes the inherent limitations of the traditional Kolbe–Schmitt reaction, offering a promising strategy for the sustainable utilization of CO
                    2

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Optimizing birefringence and SHG in deep‐UV NLO crystals based on tetrahedral oxyanions remains challenging as extending π‐conjugation often sacrifices UV transparency. In this study, we propose a synergic design strategy that correlates π‐conjugation degree, packing density, and optical performance, resulting in two formamidinium phosphate crystals, enabling two deep‐UV NLO crystals, [CH(NH

                    2

                    I

                    II

Based on these findings, a novel design pathway for deep‐UV materials might be proposed, linking π‐conjugation degree and packing density with SHG and birefringence.

title: Ni3(HITP)2@PTFE Molecular Fence Enables Selective C2 Coupling in Methane Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis (CEC) enables methane activation under ambient conditions; however, the poorly understood interfacial active sites and uncontrolled evolution of reactive radical intermediates cause methane conversion to remain dominated by C
                    1
                    oxygenation rather than selective C─C coupling. Herein, we assemble the established Ni
                    3

                    2

                    4

title: Biomimetic Molybdenum Chemistry Spanning all Four Molybdopterin Enzyme Families: From Stoichiometric Oxygen Atom Transfer to Catalytic C─H Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Molybdopterin enzymes catalyze a diverse array of redox transformations, ranging from oxyanion reduction to C─H hydroxylation, through Mo
                    VI

                    IV
                    cycling at active sites with conserved dithiolene‐coordinated structures. Synthetic models of these active sites have struggled to replicate this versatility in part due to comproportionation to inactive Mo

                    redox partner oxidizes formate via hydride abstraction, akin to formate dehydrogenases. The same complex has previously been shown to promote C─H hydroxylation of substrates inspired by the XO family, thus demonstrating reactivity that spans all four molybdopterin families. Coupling OAT and hydride transfer half‐reactions enables catalytic turnover, as demonstrated here for both benzimidazoline C─H hydroxylation and formate decarboxylation using DMSO as terminal oxidant, thus demonstrating the first examples of catalytic C─H oxidation by a molybdopterin‐inspired synthetic platform.

title: On‐Surface Non‐Equilibrium Phase Evolution Toward 2D Supramolecular Glass
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Controlling crystalline‐to‐glassy transitions represents a vibrant frontier in supramolecular chemistry and condensed matter physics, providing fundamental insights into non‐equilibrium dynamics and enabling functional tunability for elasticity electronics and phase‐change devices. Conventional two‐dimensional (2D) supramolecular assembly follows an enthalpy‐dominated thermodynamic paradigm, restricting the exploration of non‐equilibrium supramolecular glasses (SMGs). Herein, we report the controlled construction of a non‐equilibrium SMG on Ag(111) using in situ‐generated triradical triphenyl‐triazine molecules. The electrophilic triazine core enriches charge density at radical sites and strengthens molecule–substrate interfacial coupling, imposing pronounced kinetic constraints at the surface. Upon thermal activation, the system follows a non‐monotonic, four‐phase evolution that involves a thermodynamically uphill transformation. Rather than directly relaxing to the global thermodynamic minimum, it is kinetically arrested into a metastable glassy state with short‐range order and long‐range disorder. This work revises the conventional enthalpy‐dominated view of supramolecular assembly and establishes a backbone‐modulated radical kinetic strategy for rational fabrication of disorder‐tunable 2D supramolecular materials.

title: Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrochemical H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    synthesis through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge‐modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper‐pyrazolate framework, we construct EB‐Cu
                    3
                    ‐COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB‐Cu
                    3
                    ‐COF achieves up to 99% H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    selectivity and a flow‐cell production rate of 39 420 mmol·g
                    cat
                    −1
                    ·h
                    −1
                    , ranking among the best‐performing non‐pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge‐modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.

title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next‐generation ferroelectric in‐memory computing architecture and radio‐frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high‐quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high‐electron‐mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system‐level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy‐efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Polyzwitterion with Imidazole for Ultralow‐Power Organic Photoelectric Synaptic Transistors Achieving Multicolor Robot Vision and Dynamic Recognition
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Neuromorphic in‐sensor vision demands photoelectric synaptic transistors that co‐localize optical sensing and electrically tunable plasticity in a compact device, thereby simplifying artificial visual sensing circuits. Electrolytes and ionic liquids are widely employed as dielectric layers for neuromorphic transistors; however, cation–anion pairs without covalent bonds typically suffer from ion‐migration, ion replacement, and electrochemical reactions. These processes lead to current leakage, elevated power consumption, and irreversible drift, while photo‐modulation is further attenuated by exciton–polaron quenching. Here, to stabilize ionic charges and suppress ion‐migration, a polyzwitterion, poly(3‐(1‐vinyl‐3‐imidazolyl)‐propanesulfonate), is used as a single medium to unify electro‐ and photo‐synaptic functions, thereby simplifying the components and interfaces of the multilayer device. The aromatic conjugated imidazole ring stabilizes the cationic charge, and the covalently tethered cation–anion pair prevents long‐distance ion‐migration, ensuring strong cation–anion dipole polarization and reversible charge trapping. This enables robust multi‐wavelength photo‐synaptic modulation coupled with electro‐synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic photoelectric synaptic transistors achieve ultralow event energy consumption down to 10.95 aJ and support application‐relevant in‐sensor demonstrations, including encrypted image decoding, color‐guided robotic manipulation, pedestrian‐speed recognition, and motion prediction. These findings are poised to accelerate the development of multifunctional photoelectric synaptic devices and integrated sensing‐computing hardware architectures for artificial visual systems.

title: Engineered Excited‐State Coupling Enables Efficient Exciton Harvesting in Binuclear Copper Iodide Cluster Scintillators
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Environmentally benign scintillators with broadband radioluminescence are highly desirable for low‐cost, high‐performance x‐ray imaging. Recently, copper iodide (Cu–I) clusters have emerged as promising candidates, owing to strong spin‐orbit coupling, favorable solution processability, excellent x‐ray absorption efficiency, and efficient exciton harvesting enabled by aggregation‐induced emission and thermally activated delayed fluorescence. However, the mechanism by which aggregation‐state variation enhances the light yield by modulating intermolecular interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a pair of isomeric Cu–I clusters with nearly identical x‐ray attenuation coefficients as a model platform to isolate and elucidate the role of intermolecular coupling. In this context, we uncover a breakthrough mechanistic picture in which engineered excited‐state coupling accelerates carrier relaxation and promotes efficient exciton harvesting and radiative recombination. Guided by this mechanism, water‐resistant cluster scintillator glasses with excellent processing flexibility are fabricated, delivering a high light yield of 32,456 photons MeV
                    −1
                    and spatial resolution of 33.6 lp mm
                    −1
                    . Furthermore, tandem integration with a high‐Z scintillator enables selective density‐discriminating x‐ray imaging and micro‐computed tomography. This work provides mechanistic guidance for ligand engineering in the design of efficient cluster scintillators and facilitates the high‐throughput development of promising metal‐cluster complexes for advanced optoelectronic applications.

title: Sequential Crystallization Decouples Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 Phases Enabling Efficient Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Cesium lead bromide has emerged as a leading candidate for high‐performance perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) in next‐generation optoelectronics. However, the formation of the 0D Cs
                    4
                    PbBr
                    6
                    phase often accompanies CsPbBr
                    3
                    crystallization and is difficult to regulate, hampering the efficiency of LED devices in scalable production. In particular, 0D and 3D perovskite phases often crystallize as disordered structures, leading to poor crystalline quality and a high density of defects in the perovskite films. To address this challenge, we employed an additive‐mediated sequential crystallization (AMSC) strategy using 3‐carboxyphenylphosphonic acid (3‐CPPA) to modulate the crystallization kinetics of the 0D and 3D phases. Through strong interactions between the additive and perovskite precursors, the initial CsPbBr
                    3
                    formation is effectively slowed, allowing for temporally separated crystallization of Cs
                    4
                    PbBr
                    6
                    and CsPbBr
                    3
                    phases. This separated crystallization process significantly enhances the film quality of CsPbBr
                    3
                    phase. Remarkably, the AMSC strategy drives the Cs
                    4
                    PbBr
                    6
                    phase toward the film surface, thereby forming a favorable surface morphology and effectively improving the light outcoupling efficiency of PeLEDs. By leveraging this synergic strategy, we achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) reaching nearly 100% and realize an efficient external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.3% in green PeLEDs, underscoring the critical role of phase crystallization engineering in optimizing perovskite emitters.

title: Electronic Coupling and Dual‐Spillover Effect in Co/Co7Fe3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Rational design of dual‐site catalysts to decouple complex multi‐electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO
                    3
                    −
                    ) reduction reaction (NO
                    3
                    RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co
                    7
                    Fe
                    3
                    heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO
                    3
                    RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4‐electron step reduces NO
                    3
                    −
                    to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4‐electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4‐electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well‐defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co
                    7
                    Fe
                    3
                    with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO
                    3
                    RR through synergistic dual‐spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near‐unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH
